analysis:
The only changed file is docs/architecture/inference.md. Head lines 25-171 add Nemotron Super local-path documentation, and lines 890-891 are not visible in the supplied units. The diff has no code, config, or endpoint changes, so no security control changes here.

The new text describes unregistered, internal-only components: NemotronSuperLocalBridgeBuilder, NemotronSuperLocalBinding, NemotronSuperLocalLoad, NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP, NemotronSuperLocalMTP and NemotronSuperLocalPrefixCache. Per the doc it registers no model, adds no public route, and has no production caller (lines 34-35, 105, 165). It is also off by default, with MTP behind DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP=1.

Relevant to T-041 (TB-007, A-001), lines 131-145 describe a resident recurrent checkpoint bank enabled by DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1. Requests are submitted with prefix caching on and 'the local unscoped cache scope', which is not coordinator-authored. T-041 currently says production has no resident-RAM prefix cache tier and that scope is coordinator-authored from account, model build and prompt contract. That holds only while this path stays unregistered and local. If it is ever wired to coordinator or network ingress, the unscoped scope would reopen the cross-account cache reuse and TTFT oracle that T-041 says is closed.

The threat model should record this caveat when the owner is registered or wired to coordinator traffic. This documentation-only PR does not by itself make that change.

The Nemotron bounded-ingress and media-charge descriptions (lines 81-92) and the loopback HTTP statements (lines 56, 100-112) are claims. No source in this batch verifies them.

The code in provider-swift is not in the supplied evidence. A later pass should confirm the claims about the cache scope, the unwired HTTP hook, and the memory bank budget against the code.
